raw_response:
I have been working this land for over fifty years. I know Quzhou soil, I know how the seasons run here. My farm is 5 mu. My body is not as strong as it was, and there are only two of us at home now, so I cannot manage heavy work alone. I have to plan carefully.

I keep 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that is my steady food-and-cash base. Wheat goes in October after rotary tillage, I pull water from the well three times through the winter and spring. I buy improved seed from the village supply station, the kind I have used for years — no experiment. I put down base fertilizer before sowing and top-dress at jointing. Maize follows the wheat on the same ground. I do not plough again — just direct seed after harvest, saves my back and saves moisture. I use the hybrid seed everyone around here uses, Xianyu or something similar. Two irrigations are enough if I time them at tasseling and filling.

The other 2 mu I put in cotton. Cotton earns more per mu but it is punishing work — I spray many times and pick by hand. Two of us can manage 2 mu. I plough it deep in spring before transplanting. Cotton drinks a lot of water and needs potassium, I learned that the hard way when my bolls were small years back. I spray for bollworm and aphids — cannot skip that.

I do not try new things at my age. I do what I know works.
